title: Aide Signer
hello: Approve what Aide asks to sign
noHello: Set up Windows Hello in Settings › Accounts › Sign-in options (a PIN is enough), then approve again.
ownCaption: Signed with the key this computer just made
helloAfter: Windows Hello confirms after you approve
wait: Confirm it's you in Windows Hello…
matchDevice: Enter these two digits on the new device
matchMachine: Enter these two digits on the new machine
joinsDevice: Once you do, it becomes a trusted device, just like this PC.
joinsMachine: Once you do, it joins as a machine: it runs tasks and approves nothing.
passphraseAfter: Your passphrase confirms after you approve
passphraseText: It unlocks this PC’s key to sign what you just approved.
locked: Too many wrong passphrases. Try again in %s.
helloSwitch: Unlock Aide with a passphrase instead of Windows Hello
usePassphraseText: Choose a passphrase. Each approval then asks for it in this signer’s window instead of Windows Hello. Windows Hello confirms this change once.
passphraseRisk: Less safe than Windows Hello: a program running as you could in theory steal your passphrase (a look-alike window, a key logger) or guess it, so the promise that agents on this PC can’t approve on their own is weaker than with Windows Hello.
useHelloText: Enter your passphrase once more. Each approval then asks Windows Hello again, and the passphrase is no longer kept.
